episodes.213443: Abundant moisture and instability continued to feed into the outflow area from earlier evening storms.  Continued regeneration of thunderstorms resulted in rainfall from 2 to 4 inches in an hour or less.
episodes.213572: During the 3rd afternoon and evening, a warm, unstable air mass situated across central Indiana combined with an approaching upper-level disturbance, triggering scattered severe thunderstorm development. Moderate mid-level flow and strong surface heating supported localized severe microbursts as convection moved eastward through the area.||Severe storms first impacted Johnson County during the mid-afternoon around 3:00 PM EST, followed by a second round of convective activity tracking across Madison and Delaware counties between 8:00 PM and 8:45 PM EST. Estimated wind gusts reached 58-60 mph. Overall impacts were characterized by scattered tree damage, including instances of trees falling onto residential structures, along with downed power lines causing localized utility disruptions.
episodes.213626: A nocturnal convection event led to one storm moving across SNE and producing sporadic wind damage in western/central MA including downed trees and powerlines.
episodes.213679: Numerous thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening of July 3, 2026. An abundant amount of atmospheric moisture meant that these thunderstorms were capable of producing heavy rainfall which did cause some flooding of roadways, particularly across Williamson and Davidson counties. These thunderstorms also produced damaging wind gusts with several reports of downed trees and powerlines received across the area.
episodes.213781: Isolated strong thunderstorm wind gusts were recorded during the early morning hours of July 3rd, with a peak wind gust of 65 mph recorded on a personal weather station in the city of Fort Pierre, while a 62 mph wind gust was observed by the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 9 mile north northwest of Vivian.
episodes.213807: During the afternoon and evening of July 1, numerous westward and northwestward-moving storms formed across mainly the northern half of Central Alabama. These storms produced numerous instances of tree damage along with several reports of hail. Notably, golf ball-size hail fell in Hokes Bluff in Etowah County. The next two days featured thunderstorm activity mainly across Blount and Etowah counties, with minor damage, along with minor flooding in Homewood in Jefferson County.
episodes.213915: In the late afternoon of July 3, a line of storms exited Chicagoland, maintained strength across Lake Michigan and produced instances of damaging wind gusts along the Indiana-Michigan state line. A second area of isolated storms produced damaging wind gusts in Jay County.
episodes.213919: In the late afternoon of July 3, a line of storms exited Chicagoland, maintained strength across Lake Michigan and produced instances of damaging wind gusts along the Indiana-Michigan state line.
episodes.214010: Strong thunderstorms moved from southwest to northeast through Petroleum, Garfield, Daniels and Richland Counties, a few of which became severe.
episodes.214013: Very efficient and slow-moving thunderstorms brought heavy rain and flash flooding to locations in and around Glasgow. Some rainfall rates exceeded three inches per hour.
episodes.214135: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a warm and unstable airmass ahead of a slow moving cold front.
episodes.214665: A low-level trough along with low-level moisture fueled thunderstorms in southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska the afternoon of July 3rd. While storms remained sub-severe, one storm in Wyoming produced a landspout.
episodes.214673: A mid-to-upper level low pressure system stationed near the Kentucky and Ohio border began to shift northward during the morning hours of July 3, 2026 which allowed for more diffluent flow across central Pennsylvania that slowly began to erode the mid-level cap by the early afternoon hours. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms began to form during the late afternoon hours across central Pennsylvania in an environment with extremely favorable instability (3000-4000 J/kg of SBCAPE) despite having bulk shear values largely below 30 knots across the entire region. Some storms grew upscale quickly in this environment and began to turn severe given DCAPE values in the 900-1300 J/kg range by the late afternoon and evening hours. As storms shifted further southeast during the evening hours, increased moisture from the Chesapeake allowed for storms to be able to sustain themselves longer, allowing for a storm complex to begin near Williamsport and track towards Reading, producing multiple instances of tree and wire damage across Lycoming County, Columbia County, and Schuylkill County. As the aforementioned mid-to-upper level low tracked closer to the region, storms were able to fire across western Pennsylvania given the lack of previous storms. This complex tracked eastward into Clearfield and Centre Counties, producing more widespread tree damage with a measured wind gust of 61 mph at Clearfield-Lawrence Airport. Another storm complex directly behind this initial one impacted portions of far western Pennsylvania close to midnight during the morning hours of July 4, causing isolated instances of tree damage in western Clearfield County before the storms dissipated for the evening.
episodes.214789: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds, hail, and flooding as they moved over portions of northeast Illinois during the evening of the 2nd.
episodes.214790: A cluster of thunderstorms produced strong thunderstorm winds as they moved across southern Lake Michigan.
episodes.214791: A line of severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds and flash flooding as it moved across northeast Illinois during the afternoon of the 3rd.
episodes.214792: A weakening line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and localized flooding in northwestern Lake County during the afternoon of the 3rd.
episodes.214793: A line of thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts over southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon of the 3rd.
episodes.215032: A complex of severe thunderstorms moved through Northern Ohio during the evening on July 3rd. The atmosphere was unstable given the warm, moist airmass in place across the region leading to MLCAPE values in excess of 2500 J/kg and DCAPE north of 1000 J/kg. Low level lapse rates were elevated as well, around 7-8 C/km. There was weak forcing across the area leading to storms initiating off of an outflow boundary moving from the west to the east leading to damaging winds across much of Northern Ohio through the late evening.
episodes.215033: A complex of thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts across Lake Erie.
episodes.215343: Thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 3 caused at least one incidence of strong winds.
episodes.215525: While a line of thunderstorms was ongoing over far southern Michigan, spilling into extreme northern Ohio, a second area of storms was developing near Van Wert County. These storms downed a series of power poles.
episodes.215535: A weakening upper ridge combined with a weak upper level system produced fairly widespread scattered thunderstorms. Several of these storms became severe and produced heavy rainfall, yielding hail, wind damage, and minor flash flooding. Significant thunderstorm driven wind damage occurred in Anderson and Morgan counties.
episodes.215591: A severe squall line tracked from the Chicago/Milwaukee areas across Lower Michigan on Friday July 3, 2026. The line of storms accelerated as it crossed southern Lower Michigan, following a period of extreme heat and humidity that had been in place since Tuesday (June 30). This provided fuel for intensification in the form of a highly unstable atmosphere. Widespread 60 to 70 mph thunderstorm wind gusts had an outsized impact on Metro Detroit and Ann Arbor. This resulted in significant tree damage with numerous reports of trees and/or tree limbs downed onto homes, businesses, and vehicles. Nearly 400,000 Southeast Michigan utility customers lost electrical power at the peak of the outages, during the holiday weekend.
episodes.215651: Thunderstorms moving through Lake St. Clair and the St. Clair River produced wind gusts in excess of 50 knots.
episodes.215653: A thunderstorm moving through western Lake Erie produced a wind gust to 55 knots.
episodes.215664: Weak shortwaves were able to spark multiple severe thunderstorms given a highly unstable environment. MLCAPE values around 2000 J/kg with DCAPE nearing 1500 J/kg allowed storms to produce widespread damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215665: Weak shortwaves were able to spark multiple severe thunderstorms given a highly unstable environment. MLCAPE values around 2000 J/kg with DCAPE nearing 1500 J/kg allowed storms to produce widespread damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215666: Weak shortwaves were able to spark multiple severe thunderstorms given a highly unstable environment. MLCAPE values around 2000 J/kg with DCAPE nearing 1500 J/kg allowed storms to produce widespread damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215793: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed within a seasonably unstable and sheared environment during the early evening of July 3rd.  Some of the cells produced damaging wind gusts of around 60mph and a few instances of wind damage.  A storm near Flora in Clay County dropped over 2 inches of rain in just 30 minutes, leading to flash flooding and the closure of US-45.  Later in the evening, an outflow boundary triggered a broken line of thunderstorms across northern Illinois.  As the line dropped southward, a few additional wind damage reports were received along and north of the I-72 corridor from the late evening into the pre-dawn hours of July 4th.
episodes.215856: A few storms developed along a stationary boundary across southern St. Louis, Cass, and Carlton counties during the afternoon hours of the 3rd. Hail to 1 inch in diameter and multiple reports of trees down were received.
episodes.215858: An isolated thunderstorm across Itasca County produced some small hail as it moved through the area. It was able to produce 1 inch diameter hail as it moved through the Grand Rapids area.
episodes.215890: High heat and humidity amid an abnormally warm airmass and ample sunshine made for highly unstable conditions across eastern New York on July 1st and 2nd, 2026. Severe thunderstorms, forced by sufficiently robust mid- to upper-level shortwaves cresting the top of a significant ridge, consequently developed in the mid- to late-evening on both days. On July 1st, convection erupted just after 4 PM and lingered through close to 11 PM. The scattered nature of the storms led to widespread impacts noted in the Adirondacks, Mohawk Valley, Upper-Hudson Valley, Capital District, Mid-Hudson Valley, Taconics, and Mid-Hudson Valley. While some small hail was noted within a few storms, the primary hazard was wind damage. Numerous reports of downed trees and wires were therefore forwarded to NWS Albany. On July 2nd, one cluster of storms in particular developed just before 9 PM, and in reaching severe strength, led to severe tree damage in Columbia County. In fact, the town of Chatham declared a State of Emergency due to the extensive damage that led to more than 40 service calls throughout the overnight. Numerous roads were closed due to blockages from downed trees and wires, many were without power also as a result of downed trees; wires; and damaged transformers, and some in the village even lost water as the water pump station lost power and the backup generator failed. The extent of damage in Chatham led to the determination that this cluster produced winds in excess of 60 mph, with some gusts likely getting as high as 70-90 mph.
episodes.215892: High heat and humidity amid an abnormally warm airmass and ample sunshine made for highly unstable conditions across western Massachusetts on July 2nd, 2026. A cluster of thunderstorms, forced by sufficiently robust mid- to upper-level shortwaves cresting the top of a significant ridge, consequently developed and tracked into Berkshire County late that evening. Just before 10 PM, reports of wind damage were beginning to be relayed to NWS Albany from near Stockbridge. Numerous trees were downed, resulting in some road closures and a report of a maximum wind gust of 65 mph at the Pittsfield Airport.
episodes.215998: Thunderstorms developed during the early evening hours of July 2nd over far southwestern Nebraska. These storms became severe with wind gusts up to 64 MPH in Chase County and hail up to half dollar size east of North Platte. Overnight, additional thunderstorm activity developed over the eastern Sandhills and portions of north central Nebraska. A severe thunderstorm in Holt County produced a wind gust of 64 MPH north of Page.
episodes.216005: Thunderstorms developed during the mid afternoon hours over the Pine Ridge of northwestern Sheridan County. Storms quickly became severe and tracked southeast. Storms remained severe into the mid evening hours as they tracked into the northwestern Sandhills. Hail up to the size of ping pong balls and thunderstorm wind gusts to 73 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.216085: Thunderstorms produce hail up to 1.25 inches and a 64 mph wind gust over far northeast Colorado just after midnight on July 3rd.
episodes.216124: During the late afternoon and evening of July 3, 2026, thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts across eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa. The storms initiated along an outflow boundary draped across the area, a remnant of thunderstorms from the previous night. The environment was primed with ample instability (MUCAPE around 3000 J/kg) alongside modest but sufficient bulk shear of approximately 30 knots. Thunderstorms initiated during the afternoon, initially organizing into a few supercells before eventually growing upscale into a larger convective cluster.||Initial storms that developed across eastern Nebraska during the late afternoon were pulse-like in nature. Radar trends suggested a few localized downbursts, one of which led to a report of large snapped tree limbs 3 miles southeast of Omaha, NE, at 4:10 PM CST. Heading into the evening, a few supercells developed across eastern Nebraska, producing hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter in both Otoe and Lancaster counties. A few 1.00-inch hail reports were also received in and around Gretna, NE, as another supercell developed.||Later in the evening, the convection gradually grew upscale into a larger cluster, slowly pushing southward into southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa. Additional severe hail reports were received in Syracuse, NE, and Sidney, IA, while thunderstorm winds caused tree damage through the town of Cook, NE. The storms continued into northeast Kansas and northwest Missouri late in the evening, with a final 58 mph wind gust measured by the Falls City, NE ASOS at 10:11 PM CST.
episodes.216130: A man was killed by a lightning strike and three of his family members were injured at Fort Myers Beach in Lee County.
episodes.216149: Hot and humid conditions across central New York contributed to an unstable environment as an outflow boundary moved through the region during the afternoon. The boundary helped initiate scattered thunderstorms, with storms favored to become strong to severe. Dry air aloft and unstable conditions supported strong downdrafts, making damaging wind gusts from downbursts and microbursts the primary threat.
episodes.216152: Hot and humid conditions across northeast Pennsylvania contributed to an unstable environment as an outflow boundary moved through the region during the afternoon. The boundary helped initiate scattered thunderstorms, with storms favored to become strong to severe. Dry air aloft and unstable conditions supported strong downdrafts, making damaging wind gusts from downbursts and microbursts the primary threat.
episodes.216277: A hot and humid airmass remained in place across the region with scattered thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening hours. A few of these thunderstorms producing damaging winds and hail up to the size of quarters. Heavy rain fell with these storms with amounts ranging from 2 to 4 inches.  Heavy rains associated with these storms caused flash flooding in Davenport.
episodes.216290: A hot and humid airmass remained in place across the region with scattered thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening hours. A few of these thunderstorms producing damaging winds and hail up to the size of quarters.
episodes.216315: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the evening hours in northeastern Ohio and progressed into northwestern Pennsylvania. There, a very unstable airmass with MLCAPE values of 3000-4000 J/kg, modest effective shear less than 30 knots, and strong DCAPE >1300 J/kg supported single cell thunderstorms initially that produced wind damage. Another cluster of storms developed in western Ohio and tracked east into the late evening hours, still supported by the strong instability. Wind damage continued, mostly in the form of downed trees and power lines.
episodes.216328: A surge of low and mid level moisture moved into the eastern Sacramento Mountains with weak upper level flow keeping storm motion very slow. A severe thunderstorm was able to develop just west of Mayhill with one CWOP site reporting over 3 inches of rain in just over an hour leading to flash flooding in the lower James Canyon.
episodes.216334: Scattered thunderstorms moved from Montana and South Dakota into parts of western and southern North Dakota during the evening, caused by a surface trough and weak boundary. Additional supercells developed along the surface trough and produced very large hail from Divide County to Billings and Golden Valley Counties. The largest hail reported was 3 inches in diameter south of Fairfield in Billings County.
episodes.216335: Thunderstorms developed across portions of southwest and south central North Dakota during the late morning and early afternoon as an upper surface trough moved through the region. The only report of severe weather was ping pong ball sized hail in Fort Yates in Sioux County.
episodes.216367: An isolated supercell moved east across portions of northeast Colorado during the late evening hours on the 2nd. Quarter sized hail was reported in Yuma County.
episodes.216509: Active weather stretched through the Independence Day weekend amid oppressive heat and tropical moisture, leading to daily showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia. High pressure initially over the region began to condense on July 3rd, which allowed for isolated storms to form along the higher terrain. Coverage then grew in earnest on the 4th of July and then again on the 5th as convective temperatures were breached in the afternoon and scattered storms formed across the state. Storms materialized just before noon across the Kanawha Valley each day and slowly traveled eastward, causing tree and power line damage in its path. The slow movement of these storms also imposed localized flash flooding by July 5th, causing flooded roadways across parts of Boone and Logan Counties. Storms were tied to daytime heating and quickly lost composure after sunset each night as a result, bringing the severe and flooding risks to an end.
episodes.216622: From the evening hours on the 2nd through the predawn hours on the 3rd, a few clusters of slow-moving thunderstorms produced severe weather across portions of southwest Nebraska. The highlight of the evening-night was a nearly stationary supercell thunderstorm that produced up to three inch diameter hail across Hitchcock County, along with an estimated three to six inches of rainfall over northeast Dundy and northwest Hitchcock Counties. The heavy rainfall supported flash flooding across northeast Dundy County. Additional thunderstorms developed later in the night and produced a measured 59 mph wind gust in Red Willow County.
episodes.216672: An area of broad troughing developed isolated thunderstorms across Central MT. There was sufficient enough surface heating and instability to develop isolated severe hail in Fergus County.
episodes.216698: Surface heating created a corridor of MLCAPE values of 4000 J/kg from northeast Mississippi into West Tennessee on July 3, 2026. Scattered thunderstorms developed across northeast Mississippi around noon. Outflow from these storms moved northward triggering additional development across West Tennessee later in the day. A few storm produced damaging winds.
episodes.216699: Surface heating created a corridor of MLCAPE values of 4000 J/kg from northeast Mississippi into West Tennessee on July 3, 2026. Scattered thunderstorms developed across northeast Mississippi around noon. Outflow from these storms moved northward triggering additional development across West Tennessee later in the day. A few storm produced damaging winds.
episodes.216712: A volatile air mass with up to 3000-4000+ J/kg MLCAPE and 30 to 40 knots of deep layer shear developed by early afternoon over south central and parts of southeast South Dakota. Moisture pooled near a convectively enhanced outflow boundary from overnight convection, and stronger heating toward south central South Dakota broke the cap by early afternoon near enhanced convergence near Chamberlain. Initial cells were very slow moving and isolated, leading to longer-lived intense updrafts. By late afternoon, storms evolved into a broken linear structure as convection entered southwest Minnesota.
episodes.216722: A volatile air mass with up to 3000-4000+ J/kg MLCAPE and 30 to 40 knots of deep layer shear developed by early afternoon over south central and parts of southeast South Dakota. Moisture pooled near a convectively enhanced outflow boundary from overnight convection, and stronger heating toward south central South Dakota broke the cap by early afternoon near enhanced convergence near Chamberlain. Initial cells were very slow moving and isolated, leading to longer-lived intense updrafts. By late afternoon, storms evolved into a broken linear structure as convection entered southwest Minnesota.
episodes.216867: Locally induced afternoon thunderstorms over northwestern Puerto Rico during the first week of July produced strong gusts and, a funnel cloud was sighted.
episodes.216877: On July 3rd, the Storm Prediction Center placed the NWS Buffalo coverage area under a Marginal Risk for severe weather, highlighting the potential for isolated strong to severe convection ahead of an approaching mid-level shortwave. NWS Buffalo Forecast Discussions detailed that high afternoon surface temperatures interacting with moderate humidity levels created a destabilized atmosphere capable of supporting convective development. Thunderstorms initiated during the mid-to-late afternoon along localized Lake breeze convergence lines before tracking eastward into central New York. As these cells organized, the primary hazards observed across portions of Western New York, the Genesee Valley, and the Finger Lakes were localized damaging wind gusts capable of bringing down tree branches, alongside brief heavy downpours.
episodes.216878: On July 3rd, the Storm Prediction Center placed the NWS Buffalo coverage area under a Marginal Risk for severe weather, highlighting the potential for isolated strong to severe convection ahead of an approaching mid-level shortwave. episodes.216954: A few thunderstorms developed over eastern Wyoming and produced instances of large to very large hail.
episodes.216955: Severe weather impacted the Black Hills over the Fourth of July weekend. Storms brought widespread hail and isolated wind gusts that impacted some holiday festivities.
episodes.216956: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and there were some supercell thunderstorms that dropped large hail and produced very strong winds.
episodes.216965: A squall line moved across west Michigan bringing widespread 60 to 70 mph winds to a good portion of west Michigan. This followed a period of extreme heat and humidity that had been in place.
episodes.216979: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southern WI in the vicinity of a stalled frontal boundary. Some damaging wind was reported.
episodes.216986: The northern end of a line of severe thunderstorms, in the vicinity of a stationary front, produced extreme damaging straight line winds in far southern WI. 3 deaths occurred when a boat capsized on Geneva Lake. Other injuries occurred when farm silos collapsed onto motorists taking shelter from the storm. Hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted with many homes sustaining damage from the fallen trees.
episodes.216999: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms were observed across central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon and evening hours on July 4th as a typical summertime hot and humid environment was in place across the Ohio Valley. On both days, synoptic forcing was weak across the region with baggy mid- and upper-level troughing and no discernible surface boundaries present. Still, with smaller scale boundaries and an unstable environment in place, pulse thunderstorms were able to develop on July 3rd, with a few downbursts producing wind damage across western Kentucky and southwest Indiana. On July 4th, the remnants of an upstream convective system moved into central Kentucky during the evening hours. While most convection was sub-severe, one particularly strong cell produced isolated wind damage as it moved across Metcalfe and Green County.
episodes.217000: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms were observed across central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon and evening hours on July 4th as a typical summertime hot and humid environment was in place across the Ohio Valley. On both days, synoptic forcing was weak across the region with baggy mid- and upper-level troughing and no discernible surface boundaries present. Still, with smaller scale boundaries and an unstable environment in place, pulse thunderstorms were able to develop on July 3rd, with a few downbursts producing wind damage across western Kentucky and southwest Indiana. On July 4th, the remnants of an upstream convective system moved into central Kentucky during the evening hours. While most convection was sub-severe, one particularly strong cell produced isolated wind damage as it moved across Metcalfe and Green County.
episodes.217086: A stagnant weather pattern set up with hot an humid conditions and a nearly stationary weak surface trough boundary during the first four days of July. This resulted in daily, mostly diurnally driven, thunderstorms through this period.
episodes.217092: A stagnant weather pattern set up with hot an humid conditions and a nearly stationary weak surface trough boundary during the first four days of July. This resulted in daily, mostly diurnally driven, thunderstorms through this period.
episodes.217131: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the mountains of far southwest North Carolina throughout the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217265: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze collisions on several afternoons and evenings in early June.
episodes.217321: Severe weather across southern Maine on July 2, 2026, was driven by scattered multicell convection firing within an extremely hot, oppressive airmass during a record-setting regional heatwave.  Weak mid-level shortwave energy moved east out of northern New Hampshire provided convective initiation during peak diurnal heating. Deep-layer shear was marginal-to-moderate, favoring pulse severe cells and localized multicell clusters that produced damaging outflow winds.
episodes.217326: A very warm and unstable atmosphere, combined with slow-moving upper level disturbance within a weak southwest-flow aloft environment, fostered the development of slow-moving strong to severe thunderstorms which resulted in several damaging thunderstorm wind gusts, large hail, and flash flooding across mainly far southwest Kansas.
episodes.217425: A large cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms earlier in the evening left behind a large area of down shear light precipitation, strong to damaging winds, and a heat burst as temperatures warmed to the lower 90s across portions of Ness, Trego, and Ellis counties. A couple of personal weather stations recorded damaging wind gusts of 58 mph or greater from this heat burst event.

Mill Creek at Nolensville crested to 13.27 feet which was minor flood stage. At this stage, water flooded low-lying areas along the creek, including portions of Culbertson Road east of Nolensville Pike as well as walking trails near the Honey Brook subdivision. Water also approached Bluff Road west of Nolensville Pike.
